articles.title: Lauren Conrad’s ‘Laguna Beach’ family mansion, designed and built by her father James Conrad in 2004, listed for $26.5 million; inside the 8,000-square-foot oceanfront estate
articles.summary: Lauren Conrad’s family mansion, which featured in MTV’s hit reality show Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County, has hit the market for $26.5 million.
articles.body: Lauren Conrad’s family mansion, which featured in MTV’s hit reality show Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County, has hit the market for $26.5 million. The nearly 8,000-square-foot Mediterranean-style estate overlooks the Pacific Ocean from the exclusive Three Arch Bay community in Laguna Beach, California.According to Cottages & Gardens, the property was designed and built in 2004 by Conrad’s father, architect James Conrad. The home became familiar to fans through the early episodes of the reality series, which followed the lives, friendships and relationships of teenagers in Southern California. Richard Trey Dewey of Pacific Sotheby’s International Realty is handling the listing.Inside Lauren Conrad’s $26.5 million Laguna Beach mansionThe Mediterranean-style residence spans nearly 8,000 square feet and features six bedrooms, six full bathrooms and an additional half-bathroom. Its design combines Santa Barbara-inspired architecture with materials sourced from Italy, travertine flooring, arched windows and vaulted ceilings with exposed wooden beams.The home also includes formal living and dining rooms, two family rooms, a spacious eat-in kitchen with a large island and a private office. Wood-trimmed sliding glass doors, stone fireplaces and expansive terraces add to its traditional architectural appeal.According to the property listing, the rooms and outdoor spaces are positioned to take advantage of sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean and the Orange County coastline.Infinity-edge pool and private beach access add to the appealOne of the estate’s standout features is its infinity-edge swimming pool, which appears to merge with the ocean beyond. A large stone patio, towering palm trees and an expansive upper-level deck provide additional outdoor spaces for relaxation and entertaining.The property sits within Three Arch Bay, a guard-gated community known for its privacy and exclusive amenities. Ownership includes access to a private beach, clubhouse and tennis facilities.The combination of extensive land, ocean views, privacy and distinctive architecture is a major part of the appeal of the $26.5 million listing.Lauren Conrad’s family home featured in ‘Laguna Beach’Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County premiered on MTV in September 2004 and became one of the network’s defining reality shows of the mid-2000s. The series followed Conrad and her castmates through their teenage years, relationships and friendships in the affluent California coastal community.In the first episode, Conrad and castmate Stephen Colletti visit the family property while it is still under construction. The finished mansion later became part of the visual backdrop associated with the show.The series ran for three seasons, concluding in 2006. Its popularity helped launch the careers of several cast members, including Conrad and Kristin Cavallari, whose rivalry became one of the show's most talked-about storylines.In March 2026, Conrad and Cavallari reunited with other cast members for a 20th-anniversary special, bringing renewed attention to the series and its legacy.Lauren Conrad’s real estate moves over the yearsConrad has made several high-value real estate moves since her reality television days. In 2017, around the time she was expecting her first child, she listed a Pacific Palisades home for $5.2 million and a Brentwood estate for $4.5 million. Both properties reportedly sold at a profit.Conrad and her family have also maintained ties to Laguna Beach. In 2014, the Los Angeles Times reported that she had purchased an oceanfront home in the area for $8.5 million. The property was located in the Three Arch Bay community and offered views of the coastline.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: ‘Like being raped all over again’: UK detective assaulted by coworker questions probe
articles.summary: A Metropolitan Police detective who was raped by former Scotland Yard officer David Carrick has called for commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign, saying
articles.body: A Metropolitan Police detective who was raped by former Scotland Yard officer David Carrick has called for commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign, saying the force’s handling of her subsequent legal battle was “like being raped all over again”.Detective Constable Linda Williams, 60, was attacked by Carrick in 2004. She later brought a civil claim against the Metropolitan Police for failing to protect her from the serial sex offender. The case has now been settled for an undisclosed six-figure sum, with the force paying compensation without admitting liability, The Guardian reported.Williams told the BBC that the lengthy legal proceedings had been “horrific” and left her contemplating suicide. She said the “worst thing” was that lawyers representing the Met challenged the severity of her post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), arguing that she had been raped only once.“They used the fact that I just got on with my life as best I could after the rape against me,” she said, adding that her ability to continue performing well at work was cited as evidence that she had shown no signs of psychological trauma.Carrick, who served as an armed officer in the Met, was jailed in 2023 after admitting to 71 sexual offences, including 48 rapes involving 12 women. He is serving 37 life sentences. He was later convicted of further offences involving a child and a former partner.Williams reported the rape in 2021 after seeing media coverage of Carrick being charged with attacking another woman. Hertfordshire Police investigated the case and brought him to justice.In an unprecedented move for a serving officer, Williams has publicly demanded Rowley’s resignation, saying she believes little has changed in the force’s culture and that she no longer trusts the police to handle sexual violence cases appropriately.“If I was raped tomorrow, I wouldn’t report it,” she told The Guardian, citing what she described as a complete lack of empathy and support from the police.Rowley took charge of the Met in 2022, pledging to reform the force following a series of scandals, including the murder of Sarah Everard by a serving officer. A report by Baroness Casey in 2023 described the force as institutionally misogynistic.A Met spokesperson said serious flaws in the force’s handling of investigations had meant officers failed to identify Carrick’s pattern of abusive behaviour. The force said it regretted the failures and had sought to handle Williams’ claim as quickly and compassionately as possible.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2019, Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz paid $20.8 million for a glass-walled California cliff house that had originally been offered for $30 million; two years later, they revealed its transformation into an art-filled family retreat
articles.summary: Musician Alicia Keys and her husband, record producer Swizz Beatz, bought one of Southern California's best-known architectural homes for $20.8 million
articles.body: Musician Alicia Keys and her husband, record producer Swizz Beatz, bought one of Southern California's best-known architectural homes for $20.8 million (£16 million) in 2019. They paid nearly $10 million less than the original asking price before turning the oceanfront property into an art-filled family home. Known as the Razor House, the glass-and-concrete estate sits on a cliff in La Jolla, near San Diego, overlooking the Pacific Ocean. According to Architectural Digest, the 11,000-square-foot property was first listed for $30 million. The couple completed the purchase in late 2019. Two years later, the couple opened the doors of their cliffside home to show how they had turned the unusual building, which extends out over the landscape, into a peaceful retreat filled with art for themselves and their children.Engineering on the La Jolla cliffsDesigned by well-known architect Wallace E. Cunningham and completed in 2007, the Razor House takes its name from the sharp-edged coastal cliff where it stands. The building features sweeping curves, floor-to-ceiling glass walls and solid concrete beams that extend outward over the ocean.According to architectural records cited by Architectural Digest, building the home required major engineering work to secure its heavy concrete frame to the coastal bedrock. The house covers several levels linked by a glass elevator. Its design gives almost every room clear, uninterrupted views of the sea. The property has six bedrooms, a main living pavilion, an underground garage that can hold up to eight vehicles, a private cinema and a guest house. Outside, an infinity-edge swimming pool creates the impression that it drops straight into the ocean below.Curating an extensive art collectionAfter Keys and Swizz Beatz, whose real name is Kasseem Dean, took ownership of the home, they worked with interior designer Kelly Behun to bring warmth and personal touches to its modern concrete spaces. The couple used the large walls and open gallery spaces to display important works from the Dean Collection. Their private art collection includes contemporary pieces by Black artists and creators from around the world. In a feature published by Architectural Digest in late 2021, Keys explained how the home's unusual shape and design influenced their choices of furniture and artwork. "When you choose a house like this, you have to respect its architecture," Keys told Architectural Digest during the home tour. "We wanted to make sure it felt like a home, not just a museum." The interiors now feature major works by Kehinde Wiley, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Gordon Parks and Nick Cave. The couple chose low-profile furniture covered in soft, textured materials such as velvet, wool and shearling. These pieces soften the exposed concrete surfaces without blocking the coastal views.A long-cherished dream realizedSwizz Beatz revealed that he had used a picture of the Razor House as his phone's screensaver for eight years before buying it. He had admired Cunningham's architecture long before the property came up for sale. When the estate went into foreclosure and appeared on the market at a lower price in 2019, the couple moved quickly to buy it. "It's a place where you can sit and contemplate, write, and create," Swizz Beatz told Architectural Digest in the 2021 interview. He described the home as both a place for creative work and a comfortable family retreat. "It was meant to be our place of peace." The main living room, which the family calls the "Dreamland" room, features a custom piano. Keys regularly uses it to compose music while looking out over the Pacific coastline.Living in a modern architectural iconBeyond serving as a private home, the Razor House has become a well-known part of popular culture. Its futuristic design and dramatic cliffside position have led many local residents and architecture fans to compare it to the fictional Malibu mansion of Marvel character Tony Stark. The estate also has large outdoor terraces, a rooftop entertainment deck with an outdoor kitchen and private paths leading towards the beach below. Custom lighting built into the concrete structure lights up the home after dark without creating glare on its floor-to-ceiling glass walls. Property records confirm that the $20.8 million sale ranks among the highest property sales ever recorded in La Jolla. The price reflects both the lasting value of Cunningham's architectural design and the continued appeal of coastal California real estate.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Rhode Island collected more than 600 unwanted Christmas trees in 2026, but instead of sending them to landfills, volunteers are placing them along damaged streams to rebuild riverbanks and shelter young trout
articles.summary: Volunteers across Rhode Island have collected more than 600 discarded Christmas trees in 2026 to help repair damaged riverbanks and protect wild trout.
articles.body: Volunteers across Rhode Island have collected more than 600 discarded Christmas trees in 2026 to help repair damaged riverbanks and protect wild trout. The effort turns holiday waste into valuable underwater habitat for fish and other aquatic life. The statewide project, known as "Trees for Trout," is a joint effort by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM) Division of Fish and Wildlife and the Rhode Island chapter of Trout Unlimited. Instead of sending used Christmas trees to landfills, residents brought hundreds of real evergreen trees to collection events at the Arcadia Management Area in Exeter. According to event details published by the Department of Environmental Management, the trees will be reused to improve local waterways. The collected trees are being secured along damaged streams throughout the Wood River watershed. The aim is to reduce soil erosion caused by extreme weather and severe flooding.Building conifer revetments along damaged streamsRiverbank erosion has become worse along several Rhode Island waterways after powerful storms and heavy flooding. As a result, some river channels have become wider and shallower, making the water more likely to heat up. To help repair this damage, volunteers place and secure evergreen trees along eroded riverbanks. These natural barriers are known as conifer revetments. According to guidelines published by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management, the submerged trees slow the water flowing near the riverbank. As water passes through the thick evergreen branches, heavier soil particles settle out of the moving water and collect around the base of the trees. Over time, the pine needles and wood slowly break down, while the trapped soil builds up and helps rebuild a stable riverbank. This process also makes the river channel narrower, allowing the main current to flow through a deeper, cooler section.Shelter for young trout and aquatic lifeDeep, cool water is vital for wild brook trout, a native fish species that cannot easily tolerate rising water temperatures. The network of underwater branches quickly provides shelter for young fish. Juvenile trout, small aquatic insects known as macroinvertebrates, and other small water creatures use the submerged pine branches as hiding places. These natural shelters help them escape larger fish and birds that hunt them. Event information published by Trout Unlimited states that volunteers meet at the Arcadia Check Station on Ten Rod Road in Exeter before travelling to selected stream locations. Wearing waders and heavy gloves and carrying hand tools, team members secure each tree to the stream bed. They use biodegradable stakes or natural cable anchors to stop high spring waters from carrying the trees downstream. The organisation requires all donated trees to be free of artificial tinsel, metal ornaments, lighting wires and chemical fire retardants. These materials could pollute freshwater habitats and harm aquatic life.Community participation and long-term impactThe "Trees for Trout" program depends entirely on community support. Local families, environmental groups and recreational anglers take part in winter tree collection drives and summer installation events. According to the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management, reusing Christmas trees for stream restoration provides two main benefits. It keeps hundreds of large organic items out of municipal waste systems and supplies low-cost materials for environmental restoration work. Freshwater fishing generates millions of dollars in economic activity each year across Rhode Island. Financial reports from the DEM Division of Fish and Wildlife link this activity to federal restoration grants and local fishing license sales. Projects such as conifer revetments help protect wild fish populations that reproduce naturally, allowing them to survive alongside fish raised and released through stocking programs. Volunteers will continue placing the remaining collected trees along priority streams throughout the warmer months. The work will give damaged riverbanks time to rebuild naturally before winter weather returns.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Remove service road first, then build flyover, delegation tells NHAI
articles.summary: Kolhapur: Activists urge NHAI to remove the raised service road before building the Panchganga flyover, citing flood risks; collector promises design changes first.
articles.body: Kolhapur: As part of the ongoing widening of Pune-Bengaluru National Highway, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) plans to construct a strategic bridge over Panchganga river between Pulachi Shiroli and Ujlaiwadi villages, adjacent to Kolhapur city. The project is specifically aimed at preventing severe monsoon flooding on this crucial stretch of the highway.However, the project has run into local opposition. Members of Mahapur Sangharsh Samiti have expressed concern that the existing service road, which sits higher than the main highway, could act as a barrier, obstructing the natural flow of floodwater and worsening accumulation in nearby areas.A delegation from the samiti met with district collector Dr Vijay Rathod and senior NHAI officials, demanding the complete removal of existing service road before work on the proposed flyover begins. The activists alleged that the current bridge design contains critical flaws and warned that proceeding without rectifying them could trigger catastrophic flooding during future monsoons.Responding to these apprehensions, district collector Dr. Vijay Rathod assured the delegation that construction would only commence after the necessary design modifications are made to ensure public safety.Girish Phonde, coordinator of Mahapur Sangharsh Samiti, stated that the bridge proposed on Sangli Phata–Ujlaiwadi route initially featured structural elements that risked creating a dam-like obstruction. Such a barrier, he argued, would inevitably force floodwaters into Kolhapur city and neighbouring villages.“Following opposition from the local gram panchayat, the design was modified to a bridge supported by pillars. However, we recently noticed that the service road leading to the bridge is being filled up, effectively creating a massive mud wall. The design presented by the NHAI still has fundamental flaws. Infrastructure projects of this scale must be designed keeping the environmental realities of the next 50 years in mind,” Phonde said.Environmental expert Uday Gaikwad also flagged vulnerabilities in the current blueprint. He emphasised that the state irrigation department should only grant a no-objection certificate (NOC) after thoroughly reviewing the record-breaking flood levels witnessed during the 2019 and 2021 monsoons.Warning of direct action, the activists said they would physically halt the highway construction if NHAI fails to implement the required design corrections immediately.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolhapur | Silver Rate in Kolhapur | Bank Holidays in Kolhapur | Public Holidays in KolhapurStay updated with the latest Kolhapur news. articles.summary: Punjab assembly saw chaos as Congress demanded CM Bhagwant Mann’s resignation and walked out; MLA Sukhpal Khaira suspended for session over remarks.
articles.body: Chandigarh: The Punjab assembly witnessed chaotic scenes on Friday as Congress MLAs demanded chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation, stormed the well of the House and staged a walkout. In response, the House moved and unanimously passed a motion suspending Congress MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira for the remainder of the session for allegedly using objectionable language against the Chair.Wearing black scarves, Congress members arrived intent on cornering the governing party. They produced a flex-printed ‘Laanat Patra’ (letter of condemnation), accusing the govt of mishandling sacrilege cases, patronising drug and mining mafias, shielding gangsters, weakening farmers’ movement and failing to protect agricultural incomes amid rising state debt.Trouble began during Question Hour when leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa demanded Mann’s resignation. Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan asked members to reserve their issues for Zero Hour, but Congress legislators entered the well and exchanged slogans with AAP members.Appealing to the opposition, Sandhwan said the questions listed for the session concerned problems faced by the people of Punjab and urged senior Congress MLAs to set an example for first-time legislators.Amid the din, finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema clashed with Khaira and launched a scathing attack on the Congress, accusing the party of introducing “chitta”, a term commonly used for heroin. The minister also accused the Congress of taking false oaths on the Gutka Sahib, misleading people and doing politics over bodies. Congress MLAs subsequently walked out, with some tearing up and throwing papers towards the Chair.Cheema then moved a resolution to suspend Khaira, alleging that he had used derogatory language that insulted labourers, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present. He also urged the House to pass a separate resolution condemning the Congress over the alleged remarks.Reacting to his suspension on social media, Khaira said he would continue to raise issues concerning Punjab, slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota and the death of Dalit labourer Gulzar Dirba. articles.title: Kolkata Couple’s Pandal-Hopping Reel On ‘Real Happiness’ Wins Hearts Online
articles.summary: Viral Kolkata pandal-hopping reel shows a couple and son on a rickshaw, sparking online talk on “real happiness”; CESC’s Sanjiv Goenka praises the family.
articles.body: Kolkata: What defines success in life? A 20-second selfie video—capturing a simple pandal-hopping moment from a middle-aged couple’s life—that has gone viral on the internet apparently holds the answer, opine netizens.The video, which is winning hearts on the internet, shows the couple and their son smiling into a phone camera as they ride through the streets in the city on a hand-pulled rickshaw with lights dazzling in the backdrop.The video, featuring Abhishek Mukherjee, an employee of CESC Ltd, and his family has even drawn praise from his employer, Sanjiv Goenka, the chairman of RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group.Their spontaneous smiles and cheerful singalong have struck a chord with viewers, prompting conversations about happiness, family and the tendency to equate success with material wealth. Educator Amit Kilhor shared the video on X on Thursday, describing it as an example of what winning at life looks like.Calling it “Exemplar A” of how to define success, Kilhor wrote that it “should collectively be declared as the best video on Twitter for 2026”. Goenka identified Mukherjee as an employee of the group’s flagship power utility. “Some moments have a way of bringing a smile to everyone’s face,” Goenka wrote. He added, “It is heartening to see RPSGian Abhishek Mukherjee from @CESCLimited and his family capturing the joy of Pujo so naturally and winning hearts along the way.”TOI spoke to senior officials of CESC to connect with Mukherjee but he couldn’t be connected till late on Thursday. The video also triggered a wider conversation about wealth and contentment. The account peek_humour joked that Elon Musk “is still the second richest guy in the world”, suggesting that happiness cannot be measured by a bank balance.User Ritika viewed the clip as an illustration of Bengali men sharing household responsibilities and appreciating their wives’ efforts, sparking a debate about gender roles.Another user, Mishhteeee, cautioned against interpreting the family’s rickshaw ride as a sign of poverty. Pointing to Durga Puja traffic restrictions, she said a rickshaw was a practical way to get around and urged people to stop “overanalysis” of what she called “pure, wholesome family joy”.Amid Kolkata’s elaborate pandals and spectacular illuminations, the family’s simple outing offered a reminder that the festival’s happiest moments need neither grandeur nor extravagance — just the joy of being together.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: In 1990, Louisiana bricklayer Kenny Hill began a sculpture garden; by 2000, it held 100+ concrete figures and a 45-foot lighthouse built with 7,000 bricks
articles.summary: Discover the unique story of Kenny Hill's sculpture garden in Louisiana, showcasing over 100 concrete figures and a stunning 45-foot lighthouse made from 7,000 bricks. Explore the artistic expressions of faith, culture, and resilience that define this vibrant collection.
articles.body: In 1990, after settling on a small plot in 1988, bricklayer Kenny Hill started creating a sculpture garden beside Bayou Petit Caillou in Chauvin, Louisiana. Almost a decade later, the site was filled with more than 100 concrete sculptures picturing biblical figures, angels, and soldiers. By weaving his own self-portraits among these representations of Christ and lost souls, the artist became a living part of the scenes he created. According to Nicholls State University, Hill transformed the site into an artistic expression through religious imagery to personify his personal experience and understanding of life. Hill, who was born around 1950, initially lived in a tent before building a small home there. The garden was laden with American culture described in the form of inscriptions, celestial symbols, and figures. The collection eventually included cowboys, soldiers, God, and angels who were black, white, male, female, or baby.The lighthouse and figures reflected Hill’s personal visionThe most prominent feature of the garden is perhaps the lighthouse made from 7,000 bricks with sculpted figures attached to its exterior; it stands 45 feet above the property. The exterior figures include angels, soldiers, cowboys, God, and a self-portrait of Hill himself.For the figures, the principal material used was concrete, while rebar and bricks also formed part of Hill’s construction work. In terms of their arrangement, the sculptures are arranged differently from one another, as some angels appear to support or lift other figures while others stand like guards at entrances and passages. When it comes to appearance, some are depicted as barefoot; others are blue-skinned, and the rest are dressed in medieval-style clothing.Hill’s own image appears throughout the garden; in different sculptures, he is seen riding a horse, carrying Christ’s cross, or standing with long hair and a beard. One representation shows his face divided between black and white, which has been interpreted as a symbolic struggle between good and evil. However, a definitive explanation of the sculptures remains elusive, since Hill was never outspoken, and when asked by Sipiorski, an art professor, about his vision, Hill responded that he had been told to build the garden but never revealed by whom. He also recalled that Hill resisted the idea of creating art for financial gain and reportedly believed that working that way would undermine his ability to create.Abandonment threatened the garden before its preservationBy early January 2000, Hill had been evicted from the property by Terrebonne Parish for failing to cut the grass and weeds. The actual circumstances surrounding his departure remain uncertain, but the university’s account described him as being troubled when he abandoned his art and, once evicted, left on foot.Hill’s departure left the future of the garden hanging in doubt because technically his work was realised on rented land which he didn’t own. This stood true until Biology professor Gary LaFleur, who regularly passed the property while on transit to the university’s marine research station, recognised the importance of protecting the site. He contacted Sipiorski, who at the time headed the art department, and discussed ways to preserve the collection.Ultimately, their efforts led to the involvement of the Kohler Foundation, a Wisconsin-based organisation involved in preserving art environments. The property was arranged to be purchased by the foundation, which also funded a new art studio on the site. Subsequently, the foundation gifted the garden to the university. In 2002, the site officially opened to the public, and the university took responsibility for maintaining the sculptures.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1989, an Iowa farmer hit a hidden jet-engine part while harvesting corn; the discovery helped investigators probe a fatal crash and brought her a $116,000 reward
articles.summary: In 1989, Iowa farmer Janice Sorenson discovered a key engine component from United Airlines Flight 232 which aided crash investigators and earned her a $116,000 reward from General Electric.
articles.body: In October 1989, Iowa farmer Janice Sorenson discovered a titanium fan disk from the engine of United Airlines Flight 232. The discovery brought her and her husband, Dale Sorenson, a $116,000 reward from the General Electric Company, which had offered money for missing engine components following the aircraft's fatal crash in Sioux City, Iowa, on 19 July 1989.According to The New York Times, the disk was an integral part of the evidence because investigators had suspected the aircraft’s engine failure severed its hydraulic control lines. The breakthrough for Sorensons came after months of searching led by farmers and investigators surrounding the countryside for missing engine parts. General Electric had offered a total of $271,000 for the return of missing engine components, including the long-sought fan disk itself. While working on her family’s working farm, about 10 miles north of Alta, Janice struck the component with her harvesting combine.The discovery on the Sorensons' farmJanice recognised the object after her combine struck it because General Electric had circulated photographs of the missing component. She got off the machine and stopped harvesting to check whether the object was part of the crashed DC-10, which killed 111 of the 296 people aboard. After the details were verified, she contacted Jerry Clark, a General Electric safety investigator who had worked with authorities on the search.Recalling the experience to The New York Times, Janice described her immediate response: “I think I was in shock.” She recalled the moment as an emotional and tear-ridden experience that made her think of all the people who had died rather than the financial reward. The disk, however, was not the only portion recovered from the farmland near Alta; Sorenson’s neighbour, Harold Halverson, had found the remainder of the component approximately half a mile away in his cornfield.For investigators, the recovery of the disk concluded a long wait for an important component which they had long sought to examine to determine how the aircraft's engine had disintegrated in flight. The engine failure of the DC-10 had rendered the pilots without the hydraulic systems needed to control the aircraft normally and contributed to the circumstances surrounding the crash landing.Under General Electric’s reward programme, several missing parts were covered, and for the disk alone the reward stood at $50,000, as per a Los Angeles Times report from 13 October 1989. The reason that Sorensons received a larger payment was that the recovered disk was thought key to the crash.The engine evidence and the family's plansThe examination of the disk led to a finding that would shed light on a possible mechanical cause of the engine failure. On 23 October 1989, TIME reported that a crack was found by metallurgists who inspected the component, and it seemed to have been there since the start. The existence of this crack before the explosion might have triggered the plane crash; however, this was a preliminary investigative finding and not a definitive conclusion.The couple had recently sold a service station investment that had failed to produce a profit. Before completing the sale, they had been required to excavate and dispose of contaminated soil around old petroleum storage tanks, with the resulting expenses consuming the prospect of a financial return.For the Sorensons, the reward’s timing couldn't have been more auspicious as it came during a time of financial difficulty when the couple had sold off a service station investment that didn’t yield any profit. Before the sale was completed, they had disposed of and excavated the contaminated soil around old petroleum storage tanks, and the resulting expenses consumed the prospect of a financial return.Janice and Dale had married at 19 and 21 and returned to her parents' farm after Dale's Army service during the Korean War. By 1989, they were still living in the farmhouse where Janice and her father had been born. Their agricultural work included growing corn and soybeans, raising cattle and producing turkeys, while Dale had also undertaken work away from the farm.You use AI every day. articles.title: Huda Kattan bought back the investor stake in Huda Beauty after eight years; how the $6,000-startup-loan brand returned to full founder ownership
articles.summary: Huda Kattan started her beauty business with a $6,000 loan, building a cosmetics brand that would eventually attract tens of millions of followers online.
articles.body: Huda Kattan started her beauty business with a $6,000 loan, building a cosmetics brand that would eventually attract tens of millions of followers online. In 2017, the company brought in investment firm TSG Consumer Partners, which acquired a minority stake as Huda Beauty continued to expand. Eight years later, that partnership ended, with Kattan regaining full ownership of the business. As reported in June 2025, the change followed a restructuring involving Kayali, the fragrance brand co-founded by her sister Mona Kattan. The move puts Huda Beauty back under founder ownership, giving the company a different financial and operational footing as it concentrates on cosmetics.How Huda Kattan turned a $6,000 loan into a global beauty brandHuda Beauty was founded in 2013, following Kattan’s work as a makeup artist and beauty blogger. Initially, the brand became known for its false eyelashes. By giving beauty advice and product recommendations online, she created her audience and gradually turned her interest into a business.Kattan’s online presence played a significant part in the company’s growth. Her tutorials and product content helped introduce Huda Beauty to customers, while the brand developed a presence beyond social media through retail and e-commerce. By June 2025, its Instagram account had reached 54.2 million followers, according to Forbes Middle East.The business grew from its modest beginnings into an established cosmetics company. Its early $6,000 loan became part of the story of how Kattan began building the brand, although the company’s later ownership arrangements reflected a much larger operation.TSG Consumer Partners’ minority stake in Huda Beauty ended in 2025Huda Beauty entered into a partnership with TSG Consumer Partners in 2017. The investment firm acquired a minority interest in the company, giving it a stake in the business while Kattan remained closely involved in its direction and public identity.The partnership continued for eight years. During that period, Huda Beauty expanded its product offering and maintained a substantial following in a competitive beauty market. Kattan remained a central figure in the business, working alongside her husband, Christopher Goncalo, who serves as co-CEO. The arrangement ended in 2025, when the company confirmed that it had reached an agreement to bring TSG’s involvement to a close. The financial terms of the buyback were not disclosed in the Forbes Middle East report, and the amount paid for the investor’s stake was not specified.How Kayali’s separation helped reshape Huda Beauty’s ownershipThe return to full founder ownership followed a change involving Kayali, the fragrance company co-founded by Kattan and her sister Mona in 2018. In February 2025, Huda Beauty announced that it was divesting its interest in the fragrance business.Kayali moved to a separate ownership structure, with Mona Kattan co-owning the brand alongside growth equity firm General Atlantic. Mona continued as its chief executive, allowing the fragrance business to pursue its own expansion plans.The restructuring also enabled Huda Beauty to repurchase the shares held by TSG Consumer Partners. With the investor’s minority stake bought back, the cosmetics company returned to full founder ownership. The separation left Huda Beauty focused on its core cosmetics operations and Kayali operating independently under Mona’s leadership.The ownership shift leaves Huda Beauty’s leadership unchangedKattan continues to run Huda Beauty as co-CEO alongside her husband, Christopher Goncalo. Her sister Alya Kattan leads global social strategy, maintaining a role in the digital activity that has been closely associated with the brand since its early years.The ownership change did not come with an announced change to the senior leadership structure. Instead, it altered who owns the company, bringing an end to TSG’s position as a minority shareholder.In a statement reported by Forbes Middle East, Kattan said she was committed to pushing boundaries while staying true to the brand’s roots and community. The announcement presented the buyback as the beginning of a new phase for the business, although the company did not disclose the financial details of the transaction.An established brand returns to founder controlHuda Beauty’s return to full founder ownership marks a change from the investment arrangement established in 2017. Outside investors can provide resources and support for expansion, but they also acquire an ownership interest in the businesses they back. Buying out TSG has brought that shared ownership arrangement to an end.The company’s journey from a business launched with a $6,000 loan to an established cosmetics name provides the background to the decision. Its large online audience and product range reflect the growth achieved since 2013, while the 2025 transaction resets its ownership structure.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Ecuador judge orders pre-trial detention of leftist presidential candidate
articles.summary: Luisa Gonzalez, who lost to right-wing president Daniel Noboa in 2023, has called the arrest political persecution.
articles.body:
A judge in Ecuador has ordered that former left-wing presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez remain detained following her arrest for alleged money laundering.

The order on Friday came the day after 48-year-old Gonzalez, who challenged right-wing President Daniel Noboa in the 2023 election, was arrested in the rural town of Canuto.

Gonzalez, her party and her close ally, former President Rafael Correa, have called the arrest political persecution.

Several other members of Gonzalez’s Citizen Revolution (RC) party have also recently faced charges.

They include Guayaquil Mayor Aquiles Alvarez, convicted of illegally selling subsidised fuel and former Vice President Jorge Glas, serving a sentence for corruption.

Prosecutors have said that Gonzalez is one of seven people under investigation for financing the 2023 presidential campaign. The probe focuses on $500,000 poured into advertising during the race.

Gonzalez has denied wrongdoing, dismissing the charges as “absurd”.

Citizen Revolution President Gabriela Rivadeneira told a news conference on Thursday that Gonzalez’s arrest “confirms or makes visible what we have been saying lately: Ecuador is living under a dictatorship”.

Gonzalez, a lawyer and former member of Ecuador’s National Assembly, lost to Noboa in an April 2025 run-off. She rejected the result as fraudulent.

Noboa, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, later accused Citizen Revolution of conspiring to attack him.

The party has since been banned from running in local elections next month.

articles.title: China’s patrolling deviations disturb border: MEA on ITBP DG's LAC face-offs remark
articles.summary: New Delhi: Following confirmation by ITBP of the continuing India-China military stand-off on the Arunachal Pradesh border, India once again cautioned
articles.body: New Delhi: Following confirmation by ITBP of the continuing India-China military stand-off on the Arunachal Pradesh border, India once again cautioned China that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral ties, echoing PM Narendra Modi’s message to Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting last month.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time.“As we have noted in the past, the situation in India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,” ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, adding that the two sides had also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the Line of Actual Control in appropriate areas for better border management.Stronger drones must to counter PLA: ITBPThe official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control.ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapur had on Thursday publicly said that Indian and Chinese troops had lately been locked in face-offs at select points along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, which “are still continuing”. He, however, added that the ‘Shaurya’ commandos of his force, deployed along the LAC, had done an “excellent job” in dealing with the face-offs.The ITBP chief said India was focusing on building its drone and anti-drone capabilities as “conventional” military resources and infrastructure were not enough to take on the People’s Liberation Army which had undergone a massive capacity upgrade and modernisation, making China a “very strong adversary”.“Drones can pose a challenge as well as present an advantage,” Kapur said, citing the example of Ukraine and Iran which, despite being small nations and with much smaller or no conventional armed forces, had taken on superpowers like Russia and the US respectively.DG Shatrujeet Kapur said ITBP had included drone platoons for all its border units, with 70% of the Rs 400 crore allocated by MHA for modernisation of the force earmarked for upgrading drone warfare capabilities. The force is raising more ‘Shaurya’ commando platoons trained in mountain warfare, new-generation weapons and unarmed combat.Kapur said ITBP must redefine itself as a high-altitude fighting force, distinct from the Army or any other central paramilitary force.Reports of border friction coincide with the ongoing efforts to normalise Sino-India ties that have seen considerable progress since Modi’s meeting with Xi in Russia’s Kazan in 2024.In the meeting last month, Modi underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. The two leaders also expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question.Cong slams govt over face-offsCiting ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapur’s remarks about continuing skirmishes with China, Congress Friday asked PM Modi whether the pre-May 2020 status quo ante had been restored in Ladakh and if India could patrol up to border points such as Shera-5 in Arunachal Pradesh.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera said the govt should send an all-party delegation, including the opposition, to Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh to establish whether China had encroached on Indian territory.“PM gave China a clean chit in 2020. In 2026, the country deserves a clean account of what is happening on its borders. Enough of clean chits to China — it is time for govt to come clean before India.”Khera termed DG Shatrujeet Kapur’s remarks serious and claimed they showed that China’s belligerence continued despite the govt “kowtowing” to Beijing. He cited continuing skirmishes, reports of encroachment, including by BJP netas, and a trade deficit with China that had ballooned to $113 billion.Congress questioned outcomes of repeated meetings between Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping, asking why incursions and attempts to alter the LAC continued.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste have been recalled, including brands your kids may use
articles.summary: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste, including Brush Buddies Hot Wheels, Crayola and My Little Pony, were recalled. Here’s how to check your tubes.
articles.body: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste — many of them kid-themed, in flavors like bubble gum, strawberry and watermelon — have been voluntarily recalled nationwide after the Food and Drug Administration flagged manufacturing problems at the facility that made them. The recall covers several brands sold under licensed character names, along with a handful of lesser-known labels, and includes tubes with expiration dates stretching into mid-2028, meaning some of the affected toothpaste could be sitting in your medicine cabinet right now. No illnesses or injuries have been reported. Still, the FDA says families should check lot numbers and expiration dates to see whether their toothpaste is part of the recall. Below, I break down exactly which products are affected, how to tell if you have one and what to do next. Why were more than 4 million tubes of toothpaste recalled? The FDA announced the recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste distributed nationwide because of current good manufacturing practice deviations. Those are federal standards meant to ensure products are made consistently and safely, so a deviation means the manufacturing process didn’t meet requirements, not necessarily that the toothpaste itself is harmful. The voluntary recall was initiated on September 10 by Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based manufacturer, and the FDA classified it as Class II recall on October 19. A Class II recall is for products that could cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, where the chance of serious harm is considered unlikely. The FDA notice did not report any illnesses or injuries linked to the recalled toothpaste. Many of the affected tubes were marketed to kids. The recalled products include toothpaste sold under the Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels and My Little Pony brands, in flavors such as bubble gum, strawberry, watermelon, peppermint, sweet mint and cool mint. They were distributed by Ashtel Studios Inc. of Ontario, California, and come in 3.5-ounce and 4-ounce tubes, plus a two-pack of 3.5-ounce tubes. Affected products carry expiration dates from November 2026 through June 2028, and consumers should check the lot numbers and expiration dates on the FDA’s recall notice to see whether theirs is included. What to do if you have the recalled toothpaste The FDA’s recall notice doesn’t include specific instructions for consumers, and neither the manufacturer nor the distributor has issued public guidance on returns or refunds. articles.title: ‘Generation Right’: Israeli youth show strong support for the right
articles.summary: Some three quarters of Jewish first-time voters identify as right or centre-right, higher than rest of Israeli society.
articles.body:
The first Israeli elections in four years have brought with them a record number of first-time voters – most of whom are keen to make their voices count.

But while youth around the world are leaning to the left, young adults in Israel are heading in the opposite direction, according to recent polls.

The Israeli Central Elections Committee says more than half a million voters were added to the roll since the last elections in 2022. They are aged between 18 and 22 and polls show that 80 percent of them plan to vote in the October 27 legislative election .

Although their political activism and engagement in the public sphere are limited, a survey by the think tank, Israel Democracy Institute (IDI), found that a majority of young Jewish Israelis feel that the ballot box can influence reality and shape their country’s future.

But what does the future they hope for look like?

Around three quarters of Jewish first-time voters polled identified as “right or centre-right”, according to a recent poll for Israel’s Channel 12. That’s significantly higher than the rest of the Israeli population, which has already been shifting to the right for years.

Now the title “Generation Right” is being used to reference Israel’s Jewish youth – though not the Palestinian citizens of Israel.

The first Israeli elections since the October 7, 2023 attack are contentious and polarising – and they will be decisive for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political survival and his right-wing approach.

Critics of the longest-serving PM in Israel’s history accuse him of supporting “far-right” politicians to stay in power. They say that his handing of key government positions to extreme politicians such as National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich helped empower those camps and make their policies mainstream.

In 2017, Smotrich laid out his position for the future of Israel where the Israelis are the only ones who will have self-determination, whereas Palestinians will have to emigrate, stay without political representation, or be treated as “terrorists” if they refuse either of the two options. In 2022 he secured a portfolio in the defence ministry where he facilitates land grabs and empowers the illegal settlement enterprise in the occupied West Bank.

Indeed, this incitement and view of Palestinians has become more prevalent.

A recent video published by the Israeli satirist Lior Schleien shows a young man saying he would kill Arabs in Israel.

Schleien, a left-wing activist, has been visiting schools and speaking with young people often before their army service. His videos are giving Israelis, and the world, a chance to understand the younger generation.

In the video, Schleien asks the student how he proposes to kill Arabs. The answer: “Give me a knife and I will do it.”

Schleien asks whether October 7 changed his views. “I’ve always been racist,” the young man answers, adding that Arabs shouldn’t be allowed to live in the state of Israel. Even though the young man’s face is slightly covered, shielding his identity, Schleien removed the video after a public backlash.

In another town hall meeting, Schleien addresses the question of whether there are innocent people in Gaza. When asked if Israel is committing a genocide in Gaza, Schleien denies it, only for a female student to ask, “Do you think it should be done?”

Schleien looks unimpressed, but the student assures him that she is asking a serious question. Her friend, next to her, chuckles.

At a recent meeting of young supporters of the left-leaning Democrats party in Tel Aviv, 18-year-old Gili told the AFP news agency that she believed Israeli society had abandoned the idea of peace.

She said the scars of October 7 instilled fear among people, making it hard for them to believe peace could ever be achievable.

While the October 7 attack may have accelerated the country’s push to the right and far-right, many say Israeli society has been heading this way for years.

A survey by the Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth shows more than 16 percent of new voters plan to cast their ballot for far-right parties.

From a large field in southern Israel, 18-year-old Amihai was wearing a shirt with far-right minister Ben-Gvir’s photo. The event he was attending called for the establishment of illegal Israeli settlements on Palestinian territory.

Talking to other young activists from a place overlooking the destroyed parts of the Gaza Strip, Amihai said he plans to vote for Otzma Yehudit , a party led by Ben-Gvir, who himself lives in an illegal settlement in the occupied West Bank.

Although Ben-Gvir did not pass the threshold of the 2020 elections, he was given a central position in the 2022 government of Netanyahu.

In the years since, the minister seems to have learned to speak the language of Israel’s youth. Despite having been convicted of supporting “terror” organisations as well as other criminal offences, Israeli surveys show that a chunk of his potential supporters in this election are first-time voters.

Ben-Gvir has also made sure to use his position to lobby for his “I am not mincing my words” policies.

As a minister, he often visits Israeli jails and detention centres to threaten Palestinian prisoners as well as international activists – all the while making sure that it is caught on camera.

His videos often go viral, a move that has earned him more youth support – and not just from his usual base of settlers, such as the violent “Hilltop Youth”, some of whose members have been sanctioned by the European Union and the United Kingdom.

The IDI survey found that social media and messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram are key sources of information – often exposing young people to political content through their feeds rather than through active searching.

articles.title: Robert De Niro ad urges voters to vote early to avoid what Trump might 'pull on Election Day'
articles.summary: Actor Robert De Niro urged early voting in a fiery Indivisible ad, claiming President Donald Trump and the Supreme Court will interfere on Election Day.
articles.body: Actor Robert De Niro appeared in a new political ad Thursday encouraging early voting to ensure liberal votes count no matter what "they" pull on Election Day. The ad, shared by the progressive political group Indivisible, was part of a Hands Off Our Vote campaign to encourage efforts to protect the right to vote, which the "Focker-in-Law" actor claimed was threatened by the Trump administration. "Voting is a constitutional right, but you have to see that this administration and the Supreme Court aren’t paying any attention to our constitutional rights," De Niro said in the video. ROBERT DE NIRO GETS EMOTIONAL AS AMY POEHLER PRAISES HIM FOR SPEAKING 'TRUTH TO POWER' AS REGULAR TRUMP CRITIC In the ad, De Niro, a known critic of President Donald Trump, argued it should be "easy" to support any preferred candidate, whether it be a "would-be king who gets us into a disastrous war and corruptly profits from it" or "candidates who won't cut your healthcare and won't protect pedophiles." "There are some powerful people who want to take away that power. This is Robert De Niro, and I’ve got a message for them: No f---ing way. We're fighting them in the courts and standing up to them in the streets," De Niro said. MARK RUFFALO THREATENS TO 'HULK OUT' AT TRUMP, GOP OVER VOTING RIGHTS AT NYC EVENT He encouraged viewers to vote early to take back their power, suggesting that the Trump administration will likely interfere with the voting process. "Whether by mail or in person, you control when, and then, no matter what they pull on Election Day, your vote will already be banked," De Niro said. The White House responded with a scathing comment. "Robert De Niro is a washed up has-been who hasn’t been relevant in 30 years," spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital. "Now, he just beclowns himself by spewing hate speech and inciting violence against others. "Instead of embarrassing himself every time he speaks, he should immediately seek help to treat his severe and debilitating case of Trump Derangement Syndrome that has completely rotted his peanut-sized brain." Fox News Digital reached out to Indivisible for comment. De Niro's video followed months of Democratic Party members claiming Trump would attempt to "cheat" or rig the midterm elections in his favor. In a video released in August, former Vice President Kamala Harris claimed Trump and the Republicans were "trying to cheat" and that the results for Democrats must be "too big to rig." LIBERALS FLOAT TRUMP WILL TAMPER WITH, CANCEL MIDTERM ELECTIONS Republicans have called out the effort by Democrats to cast doubt on the elections while they refuse to support election security measures like the SAVE Act. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It is Democrats bending over backwards to prevent voter ID and proof of citizenship for American elections," Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, told Fox News Digital in February. "It is Democrats demanding that nobody ask questions about election security and irregularities. The projection is jaw-dropping."

articles.title: Powys runner's fitness addiction made him 'obsessive and anxious'
articles.summary: Wayne Davies was left "constantly worrying" about race times, comparing himself to other runners on social media.
articles.body:
A runner says he became so consumed by a fitness addiction that he spiralled into anxiety and became sleep deprived.

Wayne Davies said he was left "constantly worrying" about race times, training plans and fitness data and comparing himself to other runners on social media.

The 40-year-old said it felt like the "rug was being pulled from under my feet", before he was signposted to NHS Wales where he was able to regain control.

An expert said she had seen an increase in search traffic for fitness addiction in recent months as society talks more honestly about these behaviours.

Wayne, from Newtown in Powys, began running about 10 years ago as a way of keeping fit but said he reached a "real low point" at the height of his addiction as his sleep suffered, concentration declined and anxiety began to affect other areas of his life.

After starting with casual jogs he quickly progressed to marathons, before taking on ultra-distance races including a gruelling 75 miles (120km) around the Llŷn Peninsula in Gwynedd.

"I became obsessed with trying to do longer and longer distances," he said, "then I started focusing on times."

"I was never happy, and always chasing the next challenge or trying to get a better time."

To Wayne, it felt like the "end of the world" if he didn't succeed. "I never stopped to appreciate what I'd achieved," he said.

He said his struggle intensified following a heart scare during a training run, which led to him being diagnosed with atrial fibrillation - a heart rhythm condition.

Although he returned to running after treatment, he constantly worried the condition would recur, and realised it was becoming an obsession.

Wayne said he never realised a fitness addiction existed until he spoke up about it, adding that he was just trying to "get better all the time."

"Since I shared the story I've had a a lot of people saying they can relate to it," he said.

"I probably wasn't open about it before because you feel like you're going to get judged."

His friends and family encouraged him to seek help through his GP, who signposted him to the Powys-based charity, Ponthafren.

"A lot of men think talking about how they feel is a sign of weakness, and I admit I did feel a bit ashamed at first," he said.

"But taking that first step was probably the best thing I ever did."

After enrolling on the NHS Wales SilverCloud Space from Anxiety programme, he worked through a 12-week course, learning "how to manage my thoughts and let things go".

He said: "I don't tend to look at the data as much anymore. I just accept it for what it is."

He sometimes uses his watch as a guideline when running, but no longer "obsesses over it", adding that he "goes by how I feel on the day".

He has been in training for the The Marathon Eryri, formerly the Snowdonia Marathon, but with a very different outlook.

"I'm not worried about times anymore," he said. "I just want to do the best I can on the day and enjoy it."

Wayne believes more men should feel comfortable reaching out for support when they need it.

"People do want to listen and there are tools out there that can help. It's not as scary as you think."

Zaheen Ahmed, head of therapy at UK Addiction Treatment Centre, said she has seen an increase of fitness addiction cases, with more than 57,000 people seeking help from their exercise addiction page in the past six months.

"Typically this stems from clients embarking on sobriety and cross-addicting into fitness, to the point where that in itself then becomes the problem instead of substances," she said.

She said fitness apps have added a competitive element to "inform and advise" people in a way that could not be done a decade ago, but this can lead to compulsive behaviour disorder.

"If fitness has overtaken your daily joy sources, then it's likely a problem has developed," she added.

Zaheen said she did not think addictions were changing, but instead "we just have the means and desire to talk more openly and honestly about these behaviours".

"As life evolves and as a society we're exposed to more things to do, more ways to be engaged, there are more opportunities for unhealthy relationships develop."

Dafydd Judd, a personal trainer in Cardiff, said he felt the "lines are blurring" between fitness and technology addiction.

He said calorie counting apps can become "highly addictive" if you are weighing, measuring and adjusting your calorie intake.

"There's way more food to track than there is with exercise, so I can see how that can get extremely obsessive," he added.

Dafydd encouraged people to seek help if its starts to become an unhealthy relationship to ensure you are "channelling your energy in the right way".

He also advised people to be wary when seeing fitness records posted online as there are an increasing number of people "fudging the numbers and lying to to create this illusion that they're better than they are".

He described social media as a "double-edged sword" when helping people to stay fit.

"Companies are tapping into social media to help promote their business, but on the flip side, it creates these communities," he said, adding that "healthy competition" online can spur people on.

Fionnuala Clayton, project manager of NHS Wales' Online Cognitive Behavioural Therapy Service, said they were "grateful that Wayne reached out during a "challenging time in his life".

Clayton said that while exercise has mood-boosting benefits, "too much can can have negative impacts on both mental and physical health".

She said it was important to reach out for support if a routine starts to dominate other areas of your life.

"Talking to someone and exploring other sources of support can be an important step towards a healthier balance," she said.

"Stories like Wayne's remind us why accessible mental health support matters."

articles.title: Father who killed Oregon school shooter describes anguish over children he couldn't save
articles.summary: Kaylub Giamanco, has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher.
articles.body:
A father who shot dead a gunman at his two daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described "hearing children pleading for their lives" and his anguish over those he could not save.

Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by parent Kaylub Giamanco.

"I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday.

"The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save."

Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them".

He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life.

"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said.

The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was also killed, another child and a teacher were wounded.

Giamanco told OPB the day of the attack began with breakfast and packed lunches. He and his wife spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day.

The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began.

He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school.

Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

"I said, 'I'm sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die,'" he told the broadcaster.

He followed the attacker, who shot through the school's locked glass doors. Hearing children pleading for their lives and more gunfire, Giamanco crawled towards the building.

"I told myself this is probably the last thing that I'm ever going to do," he said.

Giamanco crawled through a shattered window and reached the classroom, where a teacher was struggling with the gunman. He opened the door and fired.

Giamanco told OPB he fired again when the attacker reached for his weapon. He then placed his own gun on the ground and raised his hands as an officer appeared.

He described feeling like the "last line of defence" between the children and the gunman and said he "was supposed to be there" that day.

Afterwards, he called his wife to say he would not be home for lunch and that she needed to get to the school immediately. He then called his mother to tell her what had happened.

"Mum, I just had to take the life of what I think is might be a child because he ran into my daughter's school with a gun," he said.

Police identified the gunman as Griffin J John II - a former pupil who had attended special education classes at the school. His motive remains under investigation.

Police said the teacher who confronted the attacker had thrown her phone at him, tackled him and fought to take his shotgun. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said she "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed".

The youngest victim was Rhoam Summer, 5. His father said the family was "broken and lost".

Megan Lambert, 25, the teacher who was killed, was working in what her family described as her "dream job".

"She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs," they said.

The other two boys have not been publicly named at their families' request.

The injured teacher has been named as Becky Drury, 54. She said i n a statement shared with US media that the gunman shot her as she tried to shut her classroom door.

Giamanco's name became public less than a day after the shooting. His mother, Kenda Freeman, read a family statement saying he was not seeking recognition and asking for privacy.

Shortly after the attack, Oregon Governor Tina Kotek praised his intervention while acknowledging its emotional cost.

"Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well," she said.

Giamanco told OPB he now lies awake after his family goes to bed, replaying the attack.

"I relive, I see faces, I hear voices, I hear screams."

articles.title: Harrow, Bedford: Posh British schools flock to India amid China worries and pressures at home
articles.summary: Half a dozen elite British schools are chasing growth in India amid a boom in its  wealthy population.
articles.body:
On the outskirts of Chandigarh city in India's north-western Punjab state, a 473-year-old legacy British public school opened its first all-girls international campus earlier this year.

In contrast to the prominent Gothic-style central building on the school grounds in Bedfordshire, England, the Indian premises are more modern, with purpose-built academic blocks. But a conspicuous red-brick clock tower bears the imprint of the school's British heritage.

The Bedford School, Mohali, is the newest in at least half a dozen British public schools (elite, fee-paying private schools with a long history), including three of the country's oldest, that have set up shop across the length and breadth of India. Their expansion comes amid tighter market conditions in China and the introduction of VAT on private school fees in Britain from 1 January 2025.

Since 2023, Bengaluru - India's Silicon Valley and a hub of software and start-up companies - has been home to the prestigious Harrow School, alma mater of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. Shrewsbury School has a campus in Bhopal in central India, while Wellington College has chosen to set up base in Pune, a western city that calls itself the "Oxford of the East" for its well-regarded universities and colleges.

Millfield, Queen Elizabeth's School and a few others are reportedly on their way with satellite campuses in the coming years.

For decades, India has been home to well-established local boarding schools modelled on the colonial British public-school system, serving elite, aristocratic families. But this market has rapidly expanded with newly wealthy Indian families increasingly aspiring to give their children more global exposure.

"Our international curriculum is quite a driver for many of them," Caroline Pascoe, head of school at Harrow in Bengaluru, told the BBC.

Harrow and Bedford are among the few schools in India that follow an all-through Cambridge curriculum - a global education framework recognised at 10,000 schools worldwide - from primary through to A-levels.

Harsimran Singh Kocchar, whose own extended family runs a chain of schools across India, says he decided to send his five-year old daughter Parineet to Bedford Mohali because of the "holistic focus of the school on character development, confidence and not merely academics".

He said he was also drawn to the fact the school did not have a "VIP culture" unlike many Indian equivalents.

"All kids are treated the same. Children of ministers and bureaucrats don't get greater privileges," said Singh.

Beyond the growing ranks of well-heeled local families, non-resident Indians who have either returned home after long stints abroad, or those still in the UK or Middle East wanting their children to connect to their roots, are also a significant market for these schools, says Pascoe.

Sixty per cent of Harrow's staff in Bengaluru are international and, like the others, it has imported its unique traditions to its Bengaluru campus: teachers are called Beaks, and students wear the traditional Harrow hats and uniform and take part in The Long Ducker - a cross-country race that happens across its schools globally. There is also a house system - a hallmark of traditional British education.

These quintessentially parochial quirks are blended with local customs such as singing the Indian national anthem every morning or celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi, a major Hindu festival.

While India's growing economic credentials and burgeoning population of newly minted millionaires are a natural tailwind for expansion, this growth is partly being driven by a slowdown in China.

Much of the expansion of British public schools abroad in the past decade was driven by China and Hong Kong - half of the 151 satellite campuses operated by 50 UK schools are situated in these countries.

But that growth has slowed following changes in regulation, and "increased scrutiny, and even resistance, from national governments", according to a 2025 study by the UK-based Private Education Policy Forum ( PEPF ) think tank.

A new 2024 Chinese law that required schools to integrate patriotic education into all subjects further challenged expansion and even led to planned campuses being cancelled, prompting these schools to consider other locations like India and Vietnam, according to PEPF.

Moreover, in the 2024 Autumn Budget, Britain introduced a 20% VAT on private school fees. Naomi Atkins, founding principal at Bedford School Mohali, says this has forced many private schools to look overseas.

"They are in a desperate situation. Even those that hadn't previously looked for international expansion are now suddenly active in India," she told the BBC.

But India has not been an easy market, she admits.

Most of these schools are set up in partnership with local investors or operators.

While in the past schools in other countries might have been able to do deals at 10% of revenue - the fee that they would charge the local partner-investor - margins in India may have shrunk to as low as 1% in some cases, says Atikins.

There has also been some over-estimation of the size of the market, she says.

Even though India has nearly 250 million children enrolled in schools, English education is deeply entrenched in the country and competition from local players is much more intense compared with other non-English speaking countries like China, Korea or Vietnam.

India's per capita income is also far lower and the high price-points of the British schools - which can charge up to £15,000 or more for full boarding - can limit growth.

"I've worked in Indonesia, Malaysia and China but Indians are much more price-sensitive - they like a bargain," says Atkins.

That is why Bedford Mohali has set its fees at roughly half those charged by other British schools.

Between 2011-12 and 2022-23, the satellite campuses of British schools generated £152.4m in profit, according to PEPF, and this profit has grown substantially over the years.

But in India, it appears growth is likely to be slow and steady rather than explosive.

The country's old colonial roots and new money afford the legacy institutions a significant business opportunity, but it is unlikely to be big enough to offset the loss of the Chinese market, at least immediately.
